Thanks for the ping, Soojin. I reviewed Nova's redline and the attached credit spreadsheet. High-level legal/contract guidance and proposed counter language below. I've also attached a clean countersheet draft (soojin_counter_v1.docx) with tracked changes for the Order Form.

Summary of issues we should push back on and our recommended positions:

1) Maintenance cadence & window length
- Nova asks: 1x per quarter, max 4-hour window during business hours.
- Our position: we can commit to notice and a quarterly scheduled maintenance window but need the flexibility for up to 6 hours per scheduled window for major kernel/infra upgrades. We propose: "Scheduled Maintenance: Customer will be notified at least 72 hours in advance for planned maintenance. Redwood will limit planned maintenance to no more than four scheduled maintenance events per 12-month period and, absent emergency, each scheduled maintenance window will not exceed six (6) hours."

2) Credits & ladder math
- Nova's ladder (5% @99.9, 15% @99.5) is aggressive and disproportionate for transient infra incidents; could create large credit exposure.
- We propose a three-tier ladder that mitigates tail risk: 1% credit for monthly availability <99.9%, 5% credit for <99.5%, and 15% credit for <99.0%. We also include a cap on aggregate credits per 12-month period (e.g., 50% of annual fees) and exclude scheduled maintenance and force majeure events.

3) Response times (P1/P2)
- Nova requests: P1=15m, P2=1h.
- Operationally, 15 minutes is within our NOC alerting SLA but we should limit P1 "response" to acknowledgement and initial mitigation plan within 15 minutes, with substantive updates per an agreed cadence (30/60/120 min) depending on severity. For P2, propose 2 hours for initial response.

4) Emergency maintenance carveouts
- Nova wants narrower carveouts for security patches. We can accept this but need to retain the ability to perform zero-notice emergency maintenance for critical security vulnerabilities. Proposal: require notice where practicable; for CVEs with active exploitation, Redwood may perform immediate remediation with post-facto notice and remediation report within 5 business days.

Next steps:
- Rishi: can you confirm that the maintenance window language (4 events / year, 6 hours max) and the response cadence for P1/P2 are operationally acceptable? If you think we need further caveats (e.g., blackout windows, rollover logic), flag them.
- Soojin: if Rishi signs off, I'll finalize the countersheet and we can send a consolidated counter to Nova (include the credit cap language).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: soojin_counter_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form redlines — maintenance windows & credits

Thanks — quick ops read. TL;DR: Marissa's framing is workable with a couple of operational clarifications.

Operational notes / suggested edits:
- Maintenance frequency: four scheduled events/12-months with 6-hour max each is OK for planned infra work. We should also add a clause that allows one additional scheduled window per 12-month period if mutually agreed in writing (gives flexibility for major upgrades).
- Emergency maintenance: we can support immediate fixes for high-severity security issues, but we should add a requirement that Redwood provide a post-incident remediation report with timeline, root cause, and mitigations within five (5) business days.
- Response cadence for P1: 15-minute acknowledgement is realistic given our 24/7 NOC alerts; however, we need to ensure Nova understands "acknowledgement" vs "mitigation". Recommend explicit language: "Initial acknowledgement and incident classification within fifteen (15) minutes; subsequent mitigation updates every thirty (30) minutes until resolution or handoff to engineering."
- Credits cap: ops prefers a cap on cumulative credits to avoid disproportional revenue impact from a prolonged outage; Marissa's suggestion of 50% of annual fees is OK but let's propose a smaller operational cap for early-stage customers (e.g., 35%) unless legal wants uniform approach.

We should also lock in what constitutes "availability" (metric) — e.g., exclude scheduled maintenance, provide measurement methodology (per-customer regional endpoint vs global). I'll have NOC produce a short note on measurement and blackout windows to attach if helpful.

Happy to join a quick call with Nova if Marissa/Soho want ops in the room.

—Rishi
Sr. Manager, Support & Reliability | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — maintenance windows & credits

Hi Emily — thanks for the detailed redline and the spreadsheet. We discussed internally and have attached a consolidated counterproposal (soojin_counter_v1.docx) that reflects the following compromises:

- Scheduled maintenance: Redwood will provide 72 hours' notice for planned maintenance. We propose up to four scheduled maintenance events per 12-month period; each scheduled event will not exceed six (6) hours absent emergency. We included language that permits one additional mutually-agreed maintenance window per year for major upgrades.
- Credits ladder: proposed three-tier approach (1% for <99.9%, 5% for <99.5%, 15% for <99.0%) with an aggregate cap of 35% of annual fees for early customers (Escalation: scale to 50% for enterprise deals after renewed negotiation).
- Response SLAs: initial acknowledgement and classification for P1 incidents within fifteen (15) minutes; mitigation updates every thirty (30) minutes. P2 initial acknowledgement within two (2) hours.
- Emergency security fixes: Redwood reserves the right to perform immediate remediation for actively exploited CVEs with post-facto notice and a remediation report within five (5) business days.

We believe this preserves Nova's need for predictability while allowing Redwood to operate safely. Please review the attached counter and let me know if you'd like to set up a 30-minute call this week to walk through the changes. We aim to finalize language by 12/10 to meet your sign-off timeline.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
